entries.reason: The provider identifier locates a source subject and must bind to the elected native owner without becoming a global native identity.

mapping.requirement: Scoped source-key binding to a checked owner-local catalog identity.
mapping.gap: Final source-key routing, binding uniqueness, canonical query and semantic export evidence are not qualified.

entries.reason: A subject name is a catalog named form whose script, language and evidence cannot be replaced by a raw observation.

mapping.requirement: Owner-local named forms with explicit source evidence and supported editing/query/export.
mapping.gap: Selected importer fixtures do not qualify the final native named-form contract or all downstream consumers.

entries.reason: Ordered wiki values can contain independently meaningful catalog facts and repeated qualified values.

mapping.requirement: Preserve ordered entries and map each elected semantic field to fixed native structures or governed typed assertions.
mapping.gap: Generic value-node preservation is insufficient; nested declarations and actual infobox field semantics each need independent dispositions and native query/export fixtures.

entries.reason: Historical wiki edits must preserve source revisions and support governed native adoption and restoration.

mapping.requirement: Immutable source revision evidence linked to exact native adopted revisions and restoration behavior.
mapping.gap: A stored historical wiki string alone does not prove native revision adoption, historical queries or restore semantics.

entries.reason: This is Bangumi's ranking at observation time, not an independent REZICS rank or catalog identity fact. Preserve with provider and snapshot scope; never recompute it from REZICS ratings. This disposition does not certify observation retention or export implementation.

Bangumi's source-edit lock is provider workflow metadata. It can inform ingestion evidence but cannot grant or deny REZICS authoring permissions. This disposition is a scope decision, not a claim that lock handling is implemented.
VNDB editions carry scoped participation context; they do not mandate a universal native Edition abstraction.

mapping.requirement: Represent the referent, variant and credit context implied by each scoped source entry using provider-independent native semantics.
mapping.gap: The existing software_edition slice is provisional; exact edition child paths and cross-provider/source-free semantics remain unqualified.

entries.reason: The source edition identifier qualifies a staff participation; removing it merges distinct credit contexts.

mapping.requirement: Resolve credit participation to its checked source-scoped context and elected native referent.
mapping.gap: No final native owner/field/write/query/export fixture chain is pinned for this contextual identity.

entries.reason: A staff role is a governed catalog participation meaning, not a free-form source field label.

mapping.requirement: A versioned credit-role definition and qualified participation on the correct native object.
mapping.gap: Complete role vocabulary, alias resolution, context, canonical queries and export evidence remain unqualified.

entries.reason: Release language participates in consumption availability and translation semantics independently of title language.

mapping.requirement: Scoped native availability and language roles using the pinned source-to-BCP-47 mapping.
mapping.gap: Nested language roles, qualifiers, distribution scope and native query/export roundtrips still need exact dispositions and evidence.

entries.reason: Personal list notes are user-owned activity, potentially private. Public catalog conformance neither imports them nor supplies consent for a personal-library import product. Other /ulist paths remain individually unreviewed.

An individual user's vote is user activity rather than a public catalog fact. A consented personal-history importer would require a separate contract and authorization; this scope decision excludes only this exact path.

This source database surrogate is needed to resolve MusicBrainz dump foreign keys, but must not be installed as a REZICS person/organization primary key. Resolution still requires the separate stable source identity and native binding contract.
The MusicBrainz identifier is stable source identity evidence whose native binding must respect artist person/group semantics.

mapping.requirement: A source binding to the selected person or organization owner with checked type and merge behavior.
mapping.gap: Final owner alternatives, source identifier uniqueness and edit/query/export evidence are not pinned.

entries.reason: Artist names are reusable native named forms, with aliases and credit spellings that cannot be flattened into one source title.

mapping.requirement: Person/group named-form semantics distinct from exact credited-as participation names.
mapping.gap: Complete alias, sorting, writing-system and credit-context native evidence has not been qualified.

entries.reason: The credited name preserves exact display composition while ordered constituent artist credit roles remain separately meaningful.

mapping.requirement: Native ordered credit composition with exact credited spellings, join phrases and constituent identities.
mapping.gap: Existing streamed credit fixtures do not qualify all relationships, names, canonical edits and semantic export contracts.

entries.reason: An upstream editor email is account data, outside public catalog conformance. Never import it into REZICS Auth or preserve it in a catalog raw-payload fallback.
An upstream credential is outside catalog semantics and must not enter REZICS Auth or catalog observation storage. Its presence in CREATE TABLE inventory is not permission to ingest it.
Work authorship is an ordered qualified contribution, not merely an array of upstream author identifiers.

mapping.requirement: Native book-work contributions with checked people/organization references, order and roles.
mapping.gap: The selected work import does not qualify every author-role field, native edit, query or export behavior.

entries.reason: An ISBN identifies a publication product under its own validation and scope, not the abstract work or a universal Edition entity.

mapping.requirement: Validated publication identifiers on the elected native publication/distribution referent with ambiguity handling.
mapping.gap: Duplicate or malformed source identifiers and complete native query/export evidence are not qualified.

entries.reason: Publication consumption languages must remain distinct from work origin, title language and translation provenance.

mapping.requirement: Native publication language roles linked to reviewed source language vocabulary mappings.
mapping.gap: Source vocabulary resolution, multilingual publication fixtures and native query/export coverage remain unqualified.

entries.reason: A work's origin language is distinct from the languages available on particular publications or translations.

mapping.requirement: Evidence-scoped original-language assertions separate from native publication consumption languages.
mapping.gap: Multiple origin languages, disputed evidence, canonical edits and semantic roundtrip evidence remain unqualified.
